flawed_step: Step 7: From every neighborhood of x meeting A and meeting B, it does not follow that every neighborhood meets A ∩ B; the two intersections may occur at different points.
counterexample: Let X={0,1} have the indiscrete topology {∅,X}, with A={0} and B={1}. Then cl(A)=cl(B)=X, but cl(A∩B)=cl(∅)=∅, so cl(A∩B)≠cl(A)∩cl(B).
assessment_summary:
1. Let X be a topological space and A,B⊆X. — JUSTIFIED: This sets up arbitrary objects of the quantified types.
2. Since A∩B⊆A and A∩B⊆B, monotonicity of closure gives cl(A∩B)⊆cl(A) and cl(A∩B)⊆cl(B). — JUSTIFIED: If S⊆T, every closed set containing T contains S, so cl(S)⊆cl(T).
3. Therefore cl(A∩B)⊆cl(A)∩cl(B). — JUSTIFIED: A set contained in each of two sets is contained in their intersection.
4. To attempt the reverse inclusion, take x∈cl(A)∩cl(B). — JUSTIFIED: This is the standard setup for proving cl(A)∩cl(B)⊆cl(A∩B).
5. Then x∈cl(A) and x∈cl(B). — JUSTIFIED: This follows from membership in an intersection.
6. Equivalently, every open neighborhood of x meets A, and every open neighborhood of x meets B. — JUSTIFIED: This is the standard neighborhood characterization of closure.
7. Hence every open neighborhood of x meets A∩B. — NOT JUSTIFIED: A neighborhood may meet A and B at different points, without meeting their intersection. This is the first failing step.
8. Consequently x∈cl(A∩B), which would establish the reverse inclusion and the asserted equality. — NOT JUSTIFIED: The closure characterization would support this conclusion only if Step 7 had been established.
9. To test the failed implication, let X={0,1} with topology {∅,X}, and set A={0}, B={1}. — JUSTIFIED: This is a valid topological space and two subsets of it.
10. The only closed subsets of X are ∅ and X. — JUSTIFIED: Closed sets are complements of open sets, and both ∅ and X complement each other.
11. Thus cl(A)=X and cl(B)=X. — JUSTIFIED: Each of A and B is nonempty, and X is the only closed set containing either one.
12. Since A∩B=∅, cl(A∩B)=cl(∅)=∅. — JUSTIFIED: The empty set is closed and is the smallest closed set containing itself.
13. Meanwhile cl(A)∩cl(B)=X∩X=X. — JUSTIFIED: This follows from Step 11.
14. Therefore cl(A∩B)=∅≠X=cl(A)∩cl(B). — JUSTIFIED: Steps 12 and 13 establish the inequality, so the universally quantified statement is false.
